t: Samarkand was a central city of the Sogdian civilisation and was conquered in turn by Alexander in 329 BCE, the Sasanians, the Umayyads in about 712, the Mongols in 1220 and the Russians in 1868.
Timur made it his capital in 1370 and rebuilt most of it, and his grandson Ulugh Beg built a madrasa on the Registan and an observatory there in 1428.
Under the Uzbek khans, the Russian Empire and the Soviet Union the city kept its monuments, though some were destroyed, and Persian remained its literary language.
dyk: According to legend, the secret of papermaking was obtained from two Chinese prisoners taken at the Battle of Talas in 751, which led to the first paper mill in the Islamic world, at Samarkand.
ev: Researchers date the founding of the city to about this time
Qutayba ibn Muslim captures the city for the Umayyad Caliphate
The Mongols under Genghis Khan take and plunder the city
Russian forces under General von Kaufman take the citadel
Samarkand becomes the first capital of the Uzbek SSR

f.founded: The date of founding is uncertain; researchers at the Institute of Archaeology of Samarkand date it to around 700 BCE, and it has been proposed that the city was established in the 8th or 7th century BCE.
f.where: In the valley of the Zarafshan river in south-eastern Uzbekistan, 270 km by road from Tashkent and 240 km from Bukhara.
f.known: The Sogdian city of Marakanda; conquest by Alexander in 329 BCE; the legend of the first paper mill of the Islamic world; the Mongol sack of 1220; Timur’s capital; Ulugh Beg’s observatory; the Registan, the Gur-i Amir and Shah-i-Zinda
f.today: Samarkand is the second-largest city of Uzbekistan and the capital of the Samarkand Region.
